findings.where: Screen 11 'One curve for all three', first sentence
findings.what: "The same picture fits a motor running up to speed and a tank filling" is unsourced for the tank: research-notes calls a tank level as a first-order lag only 'my reading', and a tank filling against a free outlet follows the square-root rule that lesson 4 steps as having no tidy formula. Say the condition (outflow in step with the level) or swap in a sourced example such as the cable warming or a ship answering its rudder.

findings.where: Screens 3 and 5 (the bridge from rate to decay)
findings.what: No screen gives the lesson's main reason: the rate is in proportion to the gap and the steady line holds still, so the gap obeys the discharge's decay rule and keeps the same share each τ. Screen 5 only says 'Each is 0.368 of the one before', and the reason sits in the Book's explanation, which a steps lesson never shows.

The route rests on the product rule, which none of his courses taught and which is stated in one bare line with no reason or source. It also skips the step that the slope of e^(t/τ) is e^(t/τ) ÷ τ, and the matching area rule. So 'That is the whole left side' and the integration are not earned.

findings.where: Explain (iron core), practice (Safe way first), analogy.breaks
findings.what: No quote in research.json or research-notes supports three claims: 'An iron-cored coil's L falls as its core saturates', the freewheel-diode advice, and the cable's conductor, insulation and surroundings giving 'a blend of several time constants'. Cite each at research or cut it.
The 0.05 appears after 'Take 10 out of the top' without saying it is 0.5 ÷ 10, which is L ÷ R. Screen 5 later names it τ, so add one short sentence on screen 3 to join the two.
'10 Ω' and '24 ÷ 0.5' break across lines ('10 / Ω', '24 ÷ / 0.5'), which parts a number from its unit or its divisor. Use non-breaking spaces inside each quantity.

The whole current curve is drawn while the switch in the inset is still open, so current shows before switch-on. Draw the curve behind the rider as it climbs, or close the switch before any curve appears.

SKINS.tank starts at 3 m and falls to 2 m, but its icon fills from empty up to the 2 m line, and the text says 'filling'. The share curve is the same either way, so give the skin a start of 0 m or draw the tank falling.
'A 24 V supply switches onto a 0.5 H coil and 10 Ω…' stays in place on the skin, motor and tank screens (11 to 13), where it no longer describes the picture.
The title's term 'steady state' never appears on a screen, which say steady current, line or value instead. One sentence would tie the dashed line to lesson 1's steady state, where the rate is zero.

Three things the brief promised are missing from the screens. The integrating factor ('on one screen') appears only on the Book's practice page. The sine input, whose steady state is what AC circuits found by impedance, is not mentioned. The naval single-store examples (ship answering its rudder, hydroplanes, cable warming) never reach a screen.

[^3] ('never quite reaches zero') and [^4] (the driven spring) are attached to statements, not to figures he would look up, and [^1] appears again in the bold summary. Keep the footnotes on E ÷ R and τ = L ÷ R.
